The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

# Wrapcheck

A simple Go linter to check that errors from external packages are wrapped
during return to help identify the error source during debugging.

## What is Wrapcheck?

Wrapcheck is a linter that checks whether errors from external packages are
wrapped when returned. This helps identify error sources during debugging by
adding context at package boundaries.

## Installation

Go >= v1.22.0
```bash
$ go install github.com/tomarrell/wrapcheck/v2/cmd/wrapcheck@v2
```

Wrapcheck is also available as part of the golangci-lint meta linter.

## Usage

To lint all the packages in a program:

```bash
$ wrapcheck ./...
```

## Configuration

You can configure wrapcheck by using a `.wrapcheck.yaml` file in either the
local directory, or in your home directory.

```yaml
# An array of strings which specify substrings of signatures to ignore. If this
# set, it will override the default set of ignored signatures.
ignoreSigs:
- .Errorf(
- errors.New(
- errors.Unwrap(
- errors.Join(
- .Wrap(
- .Wrapf(
- .WithMessage(
- .WithMessagef(
- .WithStack(

# An array of strings specifying additional substrings of signatures to ignore.
# Unlike ignoreSigs, this option extends the default set (or the set specified
# in ignoreSigs) without replacing it entirely.
extraIgnoreSigs:
- .CustomError(
- .SpecificWrap(

# An array of strings which specify regular expressions of signatures to ignore.
ignoreSigRegexps:
- \.New.*Error\(

# An array of glob patterns which, if any match the package of the function
# returning the error, will skip wrapcheck analysis for this error.
ignorePackageGlobs:
- encoding/*
- github.com/pkg/*

# ignoreInterfaceRegexps defines a list of regular expressions which, if matched
# to a underlying interface name, will ignore unwrapped errors returned from a
# function whose call is defined on the given interface.
ignoreInterfaceRegexps:
- ^(?i)c(?-i)ach(ing|e)

# ReportInternalErrors determines whether wrapcheck should report errors returned
# from inside the package.
reportInternalErrors: true
```

## Example

If you've ever been debugging your Go program and seen an error like this:

```log
time="2020-08-04T11:36:27+02:00" level=error error="sql: error no rows"
```

Then you know how painful it can be to hunt down the cause when you have
many methods that return errors from the same external package.

The problem is that multiple method calls into external packages (like `sql`)
can return the same error. Wrapcheck helps you enforce wrapping errors at
package boundaries to add context.

### Before (unwrapped errors)

```go
func (db *DB) getUserByID(userID string) (User, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = $1;`

    var u User
    if err := db.conn.Get(&u, sql, userID); err != nil {
        return User{}, err // wrapcheck error: error returned from external package is unwrapped
    }

    return u, nil
}

func (db *DB) getItemByID(itemID string) (Item, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM item WHERE id = $1;`

    var i Item
    if err := db.conn.Get(&i, sql, itemID); err != nil {
        return Item{}, err // wrapcheck error: error returned from external package is unwrapped
    }

    return i, nil
}
```

### After (wrapped errors)

```go
func (db *DB) getUserByID(userID string) (User, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = $1;`

    var u User
    if err := db.Conn.Get(&u, sql, userID); err != nil {
        return User{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get user by ID: %v", err) // No error!
    }

    return u, nil
}

func (db *DB) getItemByID(itemID string) (Item, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM item WHERE id = $1;`

    var i Item
    if err := db.Conn.Get(&i, sql, itemID); err != nil {
        return Item{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get item by ID: %v", err) // No error!
    }

    return i, nil
}
```

Now, your logs will be more descriptive:

```log
time="2020-08-04T11:36:27+02:00" level=error error="failed to get user by ID: sql: error no rows"
```

## Why Wrap Errors?

Errors in Go are simple values that contain only an error message. When you
call external libraries which may return errors, wrapping the error at the
call site adds additional information about where the error occurred. This
makes debugging much easier, especially when multiple calls to the same
library can return the same error.

As of Go 1.13, error wrapping using `fmt.Errorf(...)` is the recommended way
to compose errors in Go to add additional information.

func (l *loader) findListPackage(path string) *listPackage {
	if lp, ok := l.byPath[path]; ok {
		return lp
	}
	if target, ok := l.aliasTo[path]; ok {
		if lp, ok := l.byPath[target]; ok {
			return lp
		}
	}
	if lp, ok := l.byClean[path]; ok {
		return lp
	}
	for _, lp := range l.pkgs {
		if strings.HasSuffix(lp.ImportPath, "/vendor/"+path) {
			return lp
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func runGoList(patterns []string) ([]*listPackage, string) {
	if _, err := exec.LookPath("go"); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Sprintf("err: go command required, not found: %v: stderr: ", err)
	}
	args := []string{"list", "-e", "-json", fmt.Sprintf("-test=%v", flagTest), "-compiled=true", "-export=true", "-deps=true", "--"}
	args = append(args, patterns...)
	cmd := exec.Command("go", args...)
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
	err := cmd.Run()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Sprintf("err: %v: stderr: %s", err, stderr.String())
	}
	var pkgs []*listPackage
	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(stdout.Bytes()))
	idx := 0
	for dec.More() {
		var lp listPackage
		if err := dec.Decode(&lp); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Sprintf("err: %v: stderr: %s", err, stderr.String())
		}
		lp.index = idx
		idx++
		pkgs = append(pkgs, &lp)
	}
	return pkgs, ""
}

func isTestMainPackage(lp *listPackage) bool {
	return strings.HasSuffix(lp.ImportPath, ".test") && strings.HasSuffix(lp.ImportPath, ".test") && lp.ForTest == "" && len(lp.Match) == 0
}

func (l *loader) load(patterns []string) string {
	pkgs, fatal := runGoList(patterns)
	if fatal != "" {
		return fatal
	}
	l.pkgs = pkgs
	l.byPath = map[string]*listPackage{}
	l.byClean = map[string]*listPackage{}
	l.aliasTo = map[string]string{}
	for _, lp := range pkgs {
		if _, ok := l.byPath[lp.ImportPath]; !ok {
			l.byPath[lp.ImportPath] = lp
		}
		clean := cleanImportPath(lp.ImportPath)
		if _, ok := l.byClean[clean]; !ok {
			l.byClean[clean] = lp
		}
		for src, target := range lp.ImportMap {
			if _, ok := l.aliasTo[src]; !ok {
				l.aliasTo[src] = target
			}
		}
	}

	// Determine roots in the order produced by go list.
	var lpRoots []*listPackage
	seenRoot := map[string]bool{}
	addRoot := func(lp *listPackage) {
		if lp == nil {
			return
		}
		key := lp.ImportPath
		if seenRoot[key] {
			return
		}
		// The generated test-main package is not an analysis root
		// unless it was matched explicitly.
		if isTestMainPackage(lp) {
			return
		}
		seenRoot[key] = true
		lpRoots = append(lpRoots, lp)
	}
	for _, lp := range pkgs {
		if len(lp.Match) > 0 {
			addRoot(lp)
		} else if lp.ForTest != "" {
			// Packages created "for test" include ordinary
			// dependencies recompiled for a test binary.  Only
			// the external test package of a matched package is
			// itself an analysis root.
			clean := cleanImportPath(lp.ImportPath)
			if strings.HasSuffix(clean, "_test") && strings.TrimSuffix(clean, "_test") == lp.ForTest {
				addRoot(lp)
			}
		}
	}
	for _, lp := range lpRoots {
		rp := &rootPackage{lp: lp, key: lp.ImportPath, typesPath: cleanImportPath(lp.ImportPath)}
		l.roots = append(l.roots, rp)
		l.checkRoot(rp)
	}
	l.computeIllTyped()
	l.collectLoadErrors()
	return ""
}

func (a *analyzer) findAssignment(file *ast.File, target *ast.Ident) *ast.CallExpr {
	info := a.root.info
	targetObj := identObject(info, target)
	if targetObj == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var found *ast.CallExpr
	astInsp := func(n ast.Node) bool {
		if n == nil {
			return true
		}
		if n.Pos() > target.Pos() {
			return false
		}
		switch x := n.(type) {
		case *ast.AssignStmt:
			for _, lhs := range x.Lhs {
				lhsID, ok := lhs.(*ast.Ident)
				if !ok {
					continue
				}
				if identObject(info, lhsID) != targetObj {
					continue
				}
				if len(x.Rhs) > 0 {
					if call, ok := x.Rhs[0].(*ast.CallExpr); ok {
						found = call
					} else {
						found = nil
					}
				}
			}
		case *ast.ValueSpec:
			for _, name := range x.Names {
				if identObject(info, name) != targetObj {
					continue
				}
				if len(x.Values) > 0 {
					if call, ok := x.Values[0].(*ast.CallExpr); ok {
						found = call
					} else {
						found = nil
					}
				} else {
					found = nil
				}
			}
		}
		return true
	}
	_ = astInsp
	ast.Inspect(file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
		if n == nil {
			return true
		}
		return astInsp(n)
	})
	return found
}

func (p *yamlParser) parseFlowValue(tok string, line int) (*yamlValue, error) {
	tok = strings.TrimSpace(tok)
	if strings.HasPrefix(tok, "[") {
		if !strings.HasSuffix(tok, "]") {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("yaml: line %d: did not find expected ',' or ']'", line)
		}
		inner := strings.TrimSpace(tok[1 : len(tok)-1])
		v := &yamlValue{kind: yamlList, line: line}
		if inner == "" {
			return v, nil
		}
		items, err := splitFlowItems(inner, line)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		for _, item := range items {
			iv, err := p.parseInlineValue(item, line)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			v.list = append(v.list, iv)
		}
		return v, nil
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(tok, "{") {
		if !strings.HasSuffix(tok, "}") {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("yaml: line %d: did not find expected ',' or '}'", line)
		}
		inner := strings.TrimSpace(tok[1 : len(tok)-1])
		v := &yamlValue{kind: yamlMap, m: map[string]*yamlValue{}, line: line}
		if inner == "" {
			return v, nil
		}
		items, err := splitFlowItems(inner, line)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		for _, item := range items {
			k, val, found := splitYAMLKey(item)
			if !found {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("yaml: line %d: could not find expected ':'", line)
			}
			iv, err := p.parseInlineValue(val, line)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			k = strings.TrimSpace(k)
			v.keys = append(v.keys, k)
			v.m[k] = iv
		}
		return v, nil
	}
	return parseYAMLScalarToken(tok, line)
